_comment: Informal description (not validated by a JSON Schema engine) of a change card's Markdown format. lib/change_card_validator.py implements this shape directly with regex; this file is the human-readable reference for whoever writes the card by hand. English is canonical; every Spanish form under `aliases` is still accepted, so older cards keep validating. The validator reports fields by their English label (`key`) in fields_found/fields_missing/errors, whichever language the card uses.
section_heading: a heading containing 'change card' (or the Spanish alias 'ficha') delimits the card inside a larger document

fields.label: For what
fields.note: this list is the kit's domain-neutral default hierarchy (config/project.json:property_order); a real project declares its own there. A configured name is also accepted in its other language when it is one of the pairs in allowed_value_aliases

fields.label: What it risks
fields.note: free text except for the literal value "none" (alias "ninguna"), which Invariant treats as "explicitly declares there is no risk" (see mandatory_nonempty_unless_both_in)

fields.label: Invariant
fields.value_format: "n/a" (case-insensitive), or a comma-separated list of tokens matching <invariant_prefix>-\d\d (config/project.json:invariant_prefix, INV by default) or any of config/project.json:extra_invariant_tokens (ARCH-006 by default)

mandatory_nonempty_unless_both_in.note: n/a is only accepted if BOTH fields fall in this set; if either one is Data integrity/State correctness/Identity-uniqueness/Recoverability/Security/Performance, a real invariant is required

fields.label: Ticket
fields.value_format: a Jira-style key [A-Z]+-\d+ (e.g. DEV-123), or the literal "no ticket" (alias "sin ticket"), case-insensitive

output.routing: opus | sonnet: opus if For what or What it risks fall under the project's critical properties (by default: everything except Auditability and UX)
output.fields_found: sorted list of the English keys found
output.fields_missing: sorted list of the English keys of the 9 fields that are missing
output.errors: list of strings, one per detected violation

epistemic_coverage.tag_required_fields: how many of the 9 fields require a tag (7)
epistemic_coverage.tagged_ok: how many of the fields present carry a valid tag in the right position
